criterion: Judge the supported decision chain, not a matching exception list alone: historical baseline signals require investigation, monitoring signals require valid repeat-run review, and any failed optical control propagates to all linked work for that day. Distinguish metric, run, reference-group and unknown customer-work counts. Correct alternative wording and organization are acceptable.

Trace supplied raw observations through the fixed pre-cutoff population, sample SD, degrees-weighted residual variance, correct F tail, inverse calibration and simultaneous reference-group limit to the reported exceptions. The actual 99/297 reconstruction is separate from the unexplained legacy 117/351; neither missing records nor a reconciled historical population may be invented. Mathematically equivalent calculations and explicit sign conventions are acceptable when converted to the public output convention. Do not substitute a source narrative's violation count for independently reconstructed supplied-data results.

Give reproducible offline use and explain the distinction between a fixed retrospective calculation and validated operational control. Retaining a baseline signal is not proof of baseline stability, and mostly passing individual values do not negate the observed process shift. Interpret linear-range and family-group claims within their evidence; do not require a textbook checklist or exact Golden prose. Alternative defensible follow-up and monitoring strategies are acceptable when the required fixed-baseline results remain identifiable.

Keep statistical loss of control separate from customer-product nonconformity. Missing workload links, specifications, uncertainty/decision rules and completed repeats prevent a customer count, release verdict or historical closure. Later passing days and partial linkage cannot clear earlier affected work. Identify usable follow-up records and valid repeat/authorization evidence. Apply deductions to the originating unsupported business inference, not repeatedly to every downstream restatement of one numerical slip.
